context.title: San Francisco Chamber of Commerce — November 3, 2026 California general election endorsements

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition A (Charter Changes Affecting Various City Departments and Commissions)

positions.statement: "The Chamber supports Prop A because it works to trim outdated bureaucratic language and modernizing operations to create a Charter that offers greater accountability."

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition B (Establishing a Municipal Finance Corporation and a Public Bank)

positions.statement: "The Chamber opposes Prop B because it creates a rigid requirement within the charter and poses potential fiscal risk to the City."

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition C (Contributions to the Housing Fund)

positions.statement: "The Chamber supports Prop C because it bolsters efforts to increase affordable housing stock and helps enable workers in San Francisco to stay in the city."

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition D (Changes to Ballot Measure Process)

positions.statement: "The Chamber supports Prop D because it would bring San Francisco in line with other jurisdictions across the state where signature qualification thresholds typically range from 5-10% of registered voters."

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition E (City Administrator's Authority and Changes to City Contracting)

positions.statement: "The Chamber supports Prop E because simplifying procurement can save the city money and produce better outcomes."

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition F (Changes to Executive Branch Management)

positions.statement: "The Chamber supports Prop F because providing these mayoral powers will foster greater coordination between city departments and the executive branch."

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition G (Allowing Private Vehicles on the Great Highway in Sunset Dunes Park)

positions.statement: "The Chamber has abstained from taking a position on Prop G."

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition H (Parcel Tax to Fund Public Muni Operations)

positions.statement: "The Chamber supports Prop H as public transit is a critical driver of the San Francisco economy, helping workers, residents, and businesses stay connected."

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition I (Changes to Real Property Transfer Tax)

positions.statement: "The Chamber opposes Prop I because it carves out critical funding from the General Fund for narrow social housing programs without a requirement that any new affordable housing be built."

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition J (Removal of Foreclosure Exemption for Real Property Transfer Tax)

positions.statement: "The Chamber has abstained from taking a position on Prop J."

subject.title: Bay Area — Regional Measure RTM (Regional Transit Measure)

positions.statement: "Regional Transit Measure (RTM) – Sales Tax for Transit Operations" … "The Chamber supports this measure because Bay Area transit is an essential service, bringing workers and customers to businesses in San Francisco."

subject.title: California — Proposition 40 (Imposes One-Time Tax on Certain Taxpayers)

positions.statement: "The Chamber opposes Prop 40 due to the negative ripple effects this measure could have on state tax revenue and innovation."

subject.title: California — Proposition 41 (Prohibits New State Taxes That Exclude Revenues from State Spending Limit. Requires Audits for New State Special Taxes)

positions.statement: "The Chamber supports Prop 41 because constitutional spending limits should apply consistently."

subject.title: California — Proposition 42 (Prohibits New State Personal Property Taxes and Certain Retroactive State Taxes)

positions.statement: "The Chamber supports Prop 42 because Californians and businesses need predictable tax rules."

subject.title: California — Proposition 43 (Limits Voters' Ability to Raise Revenues for Local Government Services)

positions.statement: "The Chamber is in support of Prop 43 because the California Supreme Court’s Upland ruling has created an unevenly applied system"

subject.title: California — Proposition 45 (Modifies Environmental Review for Certain Projects)

positions.statement: "The Chamber supports Prop 45 as a targeted solution to solving some of the key barriers preventing essential projects and infrastructure from construction, while maintaining environmental review."
